title: Gratitude Reflection
description: Focus on the positive aspects of your day.

promptSteps.title: Notice
promptSteps.prompt: What made you smile today?
promptSteps.helperText: Small moments count here.
promptSteps.placeholder: A moment that lifted me was...

promptSteps.title: Appreciate
promptSteps.prompt: Name a person you are thankful for.
promptSteps.helperText: You can write about what they did, how they show up, or what they mean to you.

helperText: Let this be specific and ordinary. Gratitude works best when it has texture.
completionReflection: Your gratitude reflection has been saved.

title: Impostor Syndrome Unpacker
description: Examine self-doubt with objective facts.

promptSteps.title: Name It
promptSteps.prompt: What achievement are you downplaying right now?
promptSteps.helperText: Pick one specific thing, even if part of you wants to dismiss it.
promptSteps.placeholder: Something I earned or contributed to was...

promptSteps.title: Check the Facts
promptSteps.prompt: What objective, factual evidence proves you earned it?
promptSteps.helperText: Look for observable actions, preparation, feedback, effort, or outcomes.
promptSteps.placeholder: The facts that support me are...

helperText: Treat the impostor thought as a hypothesis, then check what the evidence actually says.
completionReflection: Your evidence-based reflection has been saved.

title: Worry Unpacker
description: Separate a worry into facts, fears, and the next useful action.

promptSteps.title: Worry
promptSteps.prompt: What worry is taking up the most space right now?
promptSteps.helperText: Name it plainly, without trying to solve it yet.

promptSteps.title: Facts
promptSteps.prompt: What facts do you actually have?
promptSteps.helperText: Stick to observable details and leave guesses for the next step.

promptSteps.title: Fears
promptSteps.prompt: What are you afraid might happen?
promptSteps.helperText: Let the fear be specific enough to examine.

promptSteps.title: Action
promptSteps.prompt: What is one helpful action you can take today?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose something small and within reach.

completionReflection: Your worry map has been saved.

title: What Am I Predicting?
description: Catch anxious predictions and compare them with balanced possibilities.

promptSteps.title: Prediction
promptSteps.prompt: What are you predicting will happen?
promptSteps.helperText: Write the prediction as a sentence.

promptSteps.title: Confidence
promptSteps.prompt: How strongly do you believe this prediction right now?
promptSteps.helperText: Use words, a percentage, or both.

promptSteps.title: Alternatives
promptSteps.prompt: What are two other possible outcomes?
promptSteps.helperText: They do not need to be perfect, just plausible.

promptSteps.title: Response
promptSteps.prompt: How would you respond if a friend made this prediction?
promptSteps.helperText: Borrow that tone for yourself.

completionReflection: Your prediction check has been saved.

title: Uncertainty Practice
description: Practice making room for unknowns without rushing to reassurance.

promptSteps.title: Unknown
promptSteps.prompt: What uncertainty are you trying to settle?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the question your mind keeps returning to.

promptSteps.title: Urge
promptSteps.prompt: What do you feel pulled to do for reassurance?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice checking, asking, replaying, or researching urges.

promptSteps.title: Allow
promptSteps.prompt: What would it sound like to allow this uncertainty for now?
promptSteps.helperText: Use a phrase you could repeat gently.

promptSteps.title: Values
promptSteps.prompt: What valued action can you return to instead?
promptSteps.helperText: Pick behavior that matters even while uncertain.

completionReflection: Your uncertainty practice has been saved.

title: Panic Reflection
description: Review a panic spike with body cues, thoughts, and grounding.

promptSteps.title: Body
promptSteps.prompt: What body sensations showed up?
promptSteps.helperText: Describe sensations without judging them as dangerous.

promptSteps.title: Thought
promptSteps.prompt: What did your mind say those sensations meant?
promptSteps.helperText: Capture the scary interpretation.

promptSteps.title: Evidence
promptSteps.prompt: What helped you recognize this as a wave of alarm, not immediate danger?
promptSteps.helperText: Include timing, past patterns, or what changed as the moment passed.
promptSteps.placeholder: Signs this was a wave of alarm were...

promptSteps.title: Grounding
promptSteps.prompt: What grounding helped, or what could help next time?
promptSteps.helperText: Keep it practical and repeatable.

completionReflection: Your panic reflection has been saved.

title: Safety Behavior Audit
description: Notice coping habits that lower anxiety short term but keep fear stuck.

promptSteps.title: Situation
promptSteps.prompt: What situation did you want to feel safe in?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose one recent example.

promptSteps.title: Behavior
promptSteps.prompt: What did you do to reduce anxiety or prevent embarrassment?
promptSteps.helperText: Look for checking, avoiding, rehearsing, hiding, or seeking reassurance.

promptSteps.title: Cost
promptSteps.prompt: What did this behavior cost you?
promptSteps.helperText: Consider energy, confidence, freedom, or connection.

promptSteps.title: Experiment
promptSteps.prompt: What tiny experiment could you try next time?
promptSteps.helperText: Reduce the safety behavior by one notch, not all at once.

completionReflection: Your safety behavior audit has been saved.

title: One Small Step
description: Find a low-friction action when mood or energy is low.

promptSteps.title: State
promptSteps.prompt: How is your mood affecting what feels possible?
promptSteps.helperText: Be honest and brief.

promptSteps.title: Need
promptSteps.prompt: What do you most need in the next hour?
promptSteps.helperText: Think care, movement, food, rest, support, or structure.

promptSteps.title: Step
promptSteps.prompt: What is one step so small it almost feels too easy?
promptSteps.helperText: Make it concrete enough to start in two minutes.

promptSteps.title: Support
promptSteps.prompt: What would make this step easier?
promptSteps.helperText: Change the environment, lower the bar, or ask for help.
promptSteps.placeholder: I can make it easier by...

completionReflection: Your small step has been saved.

title: Low Mood Reflection
description: Reflect on low mood without turning it into a verdict about yourself.

promptSteps.title: Context
promptSteps.prompt: What has been happening around this low mood?
promptSteps.helperText: Include sleep, stress, conflict, loss, or overload.

promptSteps.title: Thoughts
promptSteps.prompt: What thoughts are showing up with it?
promptSteps.helperText: Write them as thoughts, not facts.

promptSteps.title: Care
promptSteps.prompt: What would a caring interpretation include?
promptSteps.helperText: Make room for context and humanity.

promptSteps.title: Next
promptSteps.prompt: What is one nourishing next step?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose something supportive, not punishing.

completionReflection: Your low mood reflection has been saved.

title: Energy vs Mood
description: Separate physical energy from emotional mood to choose the right support.

promptSteps.title: Energy
promptSteps.prompt: What is your energy level like right now?
promptSteps.helperText: Describe the body first.

promptSteps.title: Mood
promptSteps.prompt: What is your emotional mood like right now?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the emotion separately from energy.

promptSteps.title: Pattern
promptSteps.prompt: How are energy and mood interacting?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice whether one is pulling on the other.

promptSteps.title: Support
promptSteps.prompt: What support fits this combination?
promptSteps.helperText: Low energy may need rest; low mood may need connection or meaning.

completionReflection: Your energy and mood check has been saved.

title: Self-Criticism Reframe
description: Turn a harsh inner judgment into a fairer, more useful thought.

promptSteps.title: Criticism
promptSteps.prompt: What is the harsh thought saying?
promptSteps.helperText: Write it in the exact words it uses.

promptSteps.title: Tone
promptSteps.prompt: What tone does this thought use with you?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice whether it shames, threatens, compares, or dismisses.

promptSteps.title: Truth
promptSteps.prompt: What part, if any, is worth learning from?
promptSteps.helperText: Find the useful signal without accepting the cruelty.

promptSteps.title: Reframe
promptSteps.prompt: What is a fairer thought you can practice?
promptSteps.helperText: Aim for believable, not sugary.

completionReflection: Your self-criticism reframe has been saved.

title: Hope Inventory
description: Collect realistic signs that change, support, and relief remain possible.

promptSteps.title: Past
promptSteps.prompt: When have things shifted even a little before?
promptSteps.helperText: Look for evidence from your own life.

promptSteps.title: Support
promptSteps.prompt: Who or what helps you keep going?
promptSteps.helperText: Include people, routines, places, beliefs, or tools.

promptSteps.title: Signs
promptSteps.prompt: What small signs of possibility can you see today?
promptSteps.helperText: Tiny signs still count.

promptSteps.title: Protect
promptSteps.prompt: What would help protect that hope for one day?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose one caring boundary or action.

completionReflection: Your hope inventory has been saved.

title: Inner Critic Dialogue
description: Create distance from the inner critic and answer it with steadier language.

promptSteps.title: Critic
promptSteps.prompt: What is your inner critic saying today?
promptSteps.helperText: Let it speak, but put its words on the page.

promptSteps.title: Purpose
promptSteps.prompt: What might this critic be trying to protect you from?
promptSteps.helperText: You can understand a protective strategy without obeying it.
promptSteps.placeholder: It may be trying to protect me from...

promptSteps.title: Impact
promptSteps.prompt: How does this criticism affect you?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice motivation, shame, avoidance, or tension.

promptSteps.title: Reply
promptSteps.prompt: What would your steadier self say back?
promptSteps.helperText: Use firm, kind, direct language.

completionReflection: Your inner critic dialogue has been saved.

title: Strengths Evidence Log
description: Use evidence from your actions to notice strengths you tend to dismiss.

promptSteps.title: Moment
promptSteps.prompt: What is one recent thing you handled, contributed, or tried?
promptSteps.helperText: Small actions are valid evidence.

promptSteps.title: Strength
promptSteps.prompt: What strength did that action show?
promptSteps.helperText: Think persistence, care, courage, honesty, patience, creativity.

promptSteps.title: Evidence
promptSteps.prompt: What concrete evidence supports that strength?
promptSteps.helperText: Point to what you did, not just how it felt.

promptSteps.title: Use
promptSteps.prompt: How could you use this strength again soon?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose one near-term opportunity.

completionReflection: Your strengths evidence log has been saved.

title: Shame Unpacking
description: Meet shame with context, accountability, and compassion.

promptSteps.title: Story
promptSteps.prompt: What story is shame telling about you?
promptSteps.helperText: Separate the story from your whole identity.

promptSteps.title: Context
promptSteps.prompt: What context does this story leave out?
promptSteps.helperText: Include pressure, needs, limits, history, or missing support.

promptSteps.title: Repair
promptSteps.prompt: Is there any repair or responsibility that belongs here?
promptSteps.helperText: Name repair without turning it into self-attack.

promptSteps.title: Compassion
promptSteps.prompt: What compassionate truth can stand beside accountability?
promptSteps.helperText: Both can be true at once.

completionReflection: Your shame reflection has been saved.

title: Comparison Detox
description: Step out of comparison and return to your own values and pace.

promptSteps.title: Comparison
promptSteps.prompt: Who or what are you comparing yourself to?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the comparison without judging yourself for having it.

promptSteps.title: Impact
promptSteps.prompt: What does this comparison do to your mood or behavior?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice whether it shrinks, pushes, or distracts you.

promptSteps.title: Values
promptSteps.prompt: What value of yours is hidden underneath the comparison?
promptSteps.helperText: Comparison often points to something you care about.

promptSteps.title: Return
promptSteps.prompt: What is one values-based action at your own pace?
promptSteps.helperText: Make it yours, not a race.

completionReflection: Your comparison detox has been saved.

title: Compassionate Letter
description: Write to yourself from the voice of a wise, caring ally.

promptSteps.title: Pain
promptSteps.prompt: What pain or struggle do you want this letter to understand?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the hard thing directly.

promptSteps.title: Ally
promptSteps.prompt: Imagine a wise ally sees this clearly. What do they understand?
promptSteps.helperText: Let the ally be kind and honest.

promptSteps.title: Letter
promptSteps.prompt: What would they write to you?
promptSteps.helperText: Use second person if it helps: you are, you can, you deserve.

promptSteps.title: Line
promptSteps.prompt: What one line from this letter do you want to keep?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose a sentence you can return to.
promptSteps.placeholder: The line I want to keep is...

completionReflection: Your compassionate letter has been saved.

title: Boundary Builder
description: Clarify a boundary and shape it into respectful, direct language.

promptSteps.title: Need
promptSteps.prompt: What need or limit is asking for a boundary?
promptSteps.helperText: Focus on what protects your wellbeing or values.

promptSteps.title: Pattern
promptSteps.prompt: What pattern happens when this boundary is missing?
promptSteps.helperText: Describe behavior, not character.

promptSteps.title: Words
promptSteps.prompt: What could you say clearly and respectfully?
promptSteps.helperText: Try: I can, I cannot, I need, I am willing to.

promptSteps.title: Follow Through
promptSteps.prompt: What follow-through will support the boundary?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose a realistic action if the boundary is ignored.

completionReflection: Your boundary plan has been saved.

title: Conflict Reflection
description: Review a conflict with emotion, interpretation, and responsibility in view.

promptSteps.title: Event
promptSteps.prompt: What happened in the conflict?
promptSteps.helperText: Describe the observable sequence.

promptSteps.title: Feeling
promptSteps.prompt: What feelings came up for you?
promptSteps.helperText: Name primary feelings beneath anger if you can.

promptSteps.title: Story
promptSteps.prompt: What story did you tell yourself about the other person or yourself?
promptSteps.helperText: This is the interpretation layer.

promptSteps.title: Next
promptSteps.prompt: What is the next constructive move?
promptSteps.helperText: Consider pausing, clarifying, apologizing, or asking directly.

completionReflection: Your conflict reflection has been saved.

title: Needs & Requests
description: Translate a relationship need into a specific, doable request.

promptSteps.title: Feeling
promptSteps.prompt: What feeling tells you a need is present?
promptSteps.helperText: Feelings can point to needs without making anyone wrong.

promptSteps.title: Need
promptSteps.prompt: What need is underneath this feeling?
promptSteps.helperText: Try support, space, reassurance, honesty, respect, or collaboration.

promptSteps.title: Request
promptSteps.prompt: What specific request could you make?
promptSteps.helperText: Make it observable and time-bound if possible.

promptSteps.title: Flexibility
promptSteps.prompt: Where can you stay flexible while still honoring the need?
promptSteps.helperText: Separate the need from one exact strategy.

completionReflection: Your needs and requests reflection has been saved.

title: Relationship Trigger Reflection
description: Understand a relational trigger before choosing how to respond.

promptSteps.title: Trigger
promptSteps.prompt: What moment felt triggering?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose the smallest specific moment.

promptSteps.title: Body
promptSteps.prompt: What happened in your body?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice activation, shutdown, heat, tension, or numbness.

promptSteps.title: Meaning
promptSteps.prompt: What meaning did your mind attach to it?
promptSteps.helperText: This may be old, new, accurate, or incomplete.

promptSteps.title: Choice
promptSteps.prompt: What response would align with your values?
promptSteps.helperText: Give yourself a choice between reaction and response.

completionReflection: Your trigger reflection has been saved.

title: Repair Conversation Prep
description: Prepare for a conversation that repairs trust or clears the air.

promptSteps.title: Goal
promptSteps.prompt: What do you want this conversation to make possible?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the relationship outcome, not just the point you want to prove.

promptSteps.title: Own
promptSteps.prompt: What part can you own without over-owning?
promptSteps.helperText: Accountability is specific, not global self-blame.

promptSteps.title: Hear
promptSteps.prompt: What do you need to hear or understand from them?
promptSteps.helperText: Turn assumptions into questions.

promptSteps.title: Opening
promptSteps.prompt: What opening sentence could start the repair?
promptSteps.helperText: Keep it direct and non-accusing.

completionReflection: Your repair conversation prep has been saved.

title: Avoidance Map
description: Map what you avoid, what it protects, and what it costs.

promptSteps.title: Task
promptSteps.prompt: What are you avoiding?
promptSteps.helperText: Name one task, decision, message, or situation.

promptSteps.title: Feeling
promptSteps.prompt: What feeling does avoidance protect you from?
promptSteps.helperText: Look for fear, shame, boredom, uncertainty, or overwhelm.

promptSteps.title: Cost
promptSteps.prompt: What does avoidance cost if it continues?
promptSteps.helperText: Consider stress, trust, time, opportunity, or self-respect.

promptSteps.title: Approach
promptSteps.prompt: What is the smallest approach step?
promptSteps.helperText: Make it easier than your mind thinks it should be.

completionReflection: Your avoidance map has been saved.

title: Procrastination Unpacker
description: Understand the friction behind procrastination and lower the start cost.

promptSteps.title: Target
promptSteps.prompt: What task are you putting off?
promptSteps.helperText: Pick one concrete target.

promptSteps.title: Block
promptSteps.prompt: What makes starting feel hard?
promptSteps.helperText: Look for unclear steps, fear, perfectionism, resentment, or fatigue.

promptSteps.title: Lower Bar
promptSteps.prompt: How could you lower the bar without quitting?
promptSteps.helperText: Shrink the scope, time, or quality demand.
promptSteps.placeholder: I could lower the bar by...

promptSteps.title: Start
promptSteps.prompt: What is your first two-minute move?
promptSteps.helperText: The goal is contact with the task.

completionReflection: Your procrastination reflection has been saved.

title: Task Breakdown
description: Turn an overwhelming task into visible, doable pieces.

promptSteps.title: Task
promptSteps.prompt: What task feels too big?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the outcome you are trying to reach.

promptSteps.title: Parts
promptSteps.prompt: What are the smallest visible parts of this task?
promptSteps.helperText: List pieces that can be checked off.

promptSteps.title: First
promptSteps.prompt: Which part should happen first?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose the part that unlocks the next move.

promptSteps.title: Done
promptSteps.prompt: What will count as enough for today?
promptSteps.helperText: Define a stopping point before you start.

completionReflection: Your task breakdown has been saved.

title: Perfectionism Reframe
description: Loosen impossible standards while keeping care and quality.

promptSteps.title: Standard
promptSteps.prompt: What standard are you trying to meet?
promptSteps.helperText: Write the rule your mind is using.

promptSteps.title: Cost
promptSteps.prompt: What does this standard cost you?
promptSteps.helperText: Consider delays, stress, avoidance, or lost creativity.

promptSteps.title: Good Enough
promptSteps.prompt: What would good enough look like?
promptSteps.helperText: Good enough can still be responsible and thoughtful.

promptSteps.title: Practice
promptSteps.prompt: What is one place to practice good enough?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose a low-risk experiment.

completionReflection: Your perfectionism reframe has been saved.

title: Decision Journal
description: Clarify a decision by naming values, tradeoffs, and next information.

promptSteps.title: Decision
promptSteps.prompt: What decision are you facing?
promptSteps.helperText: Write the choice as clearly as possible.

promptSteps.title: Values
promptSteps.prompt: What values matter in this decision?
promptSteps.helperText: Think health, honesty, growth, stability, care, freedom, or connection.

promptSteps.title: Tradeoffs
promptSteps.prompt: What are the real tradeoffs?
promptSteps.helperText: Every option gives and costs something.

promptSteps.title: Next
promptSteps.prompt: What information or action would help you decide?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose one next move, not the whole answer.

completionReflection: Your decision journal has been saved.

title: Values Check-In
description: Reconnect with what matters and choose a values-aligned action.

promptSteps.title: Value
promptSteps.prompt: What value wants more attention right now?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose one value, not a whole life plan.
promptSteps.placeholder: A value I care about is...

promptSteps.title: Why
promptSteps.prompt: Why does this value matter to you?
promptSteps.helperText: Let your answer be personal.

promptSteps.title: Drift
promptSteps.prompt: Where have you drifted from this value?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice without scolding yourself.

promptSteps.title: Action
promptSteps.prompt: What small action would move toward it?
promptSteps.helperText: Make it specific and doable today.
promptSteps.placeholder: I can move toward it by...

completionReflection: Your values check-in has been saved.

title: Control vs Influence
description: Sort what you can control, influence, or release for now.

promptSteps.title: Concern
promptSteps.prompt: What concern are you carrying?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the situation or outcome.

promptSteps.title: Control
promptSteps.prompt: What is directly within your control?
promptSteps.helperText: Focus on your actions, words, attention, and boundaries.

promptSteps.title: Influence
promptSteps.prompt: What can you influence but not force?
promptSteps.helperText: This is where effort matters but outcomes stay shared.

promptSteps.title: Release
promptSteps.prompt: What can you practice releasing for now?
promptSteps.helperText: Release means unclenching, not pretending not to care.

completionReflection: Your control and influence map has been saved.

title: Sleep Wind-Down Reflection
description: Set down the day and prepare your mind for rest.

promptSteps.title: Day
promptSteps.prompt: What from today is still active in your mind?
promptSteps.helperText: List it so your mind does not have to hold it alone.

promptSteps.title: Complete
promptSteps.prompt: What is complete enough for today?
promptSteps.helperText: Mark a stopping point.

promptSteps.title: Tomorrow
promptSteps.prompt: What can wait until tomorrow?
promptSteps.helperText: Place it outside tonight.

promptSteps.title: Rest
promptSteps.prompt: What restful cue can you give your body now?
promptSteps.helperText: Think light, breath, temperature, sound, or posture.

completionReflection: Your wind-down reflection has been saved.

title: Burnout Check-In
description: Assess depletion, pressure, and one boundary that protects recovery.

promptSteps.title: Signals
promptSteps.prompt: What signs of depletion are showing up?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice body, mood, attention, cynicism, or irritability.

promptSteps.title: Pressure
promptSteps.prompt: What pressure is weighing most heavily?
promptSteps.helperText: Name the demand or expectation.

promptSteps.title: Need
promptSteps.prompt: What recovery need is being underfed?
promptSteps.helperText: Think rest, autonomy, meaning, connection, movement, or quiet.

promptSteps.title: Boundary
promptSteps.prompt: What boundary or reduction would help this week?
promptSteps.helperText: Choose a real adjustment, even a small one.

completionReflection: Your burnout check-in has been saved.

title: Three Good Things
description: Record three good things and why they mattered.

promptSteps.title: First
promptSteps.prompt: What is one good thing from today?
promptSteps.helperText: It can be tiny, practical, or emotional.

promptSteps.title: Meaning
promptSteps.prompt: Why did this good thing matter?
promptSteps.helperText: Notice the need, value, or feeling it touched.

promptSteps.title: More Good
promptSteps.prompt: What are two more good things from today?
promptSteps.helperText: Let ordinary things count.

promptSteps.title: Savor
promptSteps.prompt: How do these good things feel in your body or mood?
promptSteps.helperText: Pause long enough to register them.

completionReflection: Your three good things reflection has been saved.
